title: Judicializacao da saude consome R$ 1,84 bilhao com dez medicamentos mais caros
summary: R$1.84 billion spent on just ten judicially ordered medications. R$2.7 billion annual bill equals one-third of Mais Medicos, nearly half of Brasil Sorridente, one-fifth of immunization program, and the entire SAMU budget -- serving only 6,000 patients.

title: Judicializacao representa um terco do gasto estadual com medicamentos
summary: IPEA study: judicialized medication spending averaged 32.9% of total state medication budgets in 2023. New health lawsuits jumped from 76,836 in 2020 to 162,046 in 2024 (110.9% increase).

title: Judicializacao corresponde a quase 33% dos gastos em medicamentos de estados brasileiros
summary: Municipalities increased medication spending by 40% vs 2019 while federal transfers fell 21% and state transfers fell 22%. Small municipalities (under 5,000 inhabitants) had highest per capita judicial medication cost at R$81.75.

title: Ministerio Saude paga R$ 2,7 bilhoes com medicamentos judicializados e teme explosao de custos
summary: Ministry of Health spent R$2.73 billion on judicially ordered medications in 2024, up from R$1.8 billion in 2022 (50% increase in two years). Gene therapy Elevidys (R$14.6 million/patient) could cause cost explosion -- R$3 billion estimated for 213 patients with active lawsuits.

title: Municipio banca mais de 80% dos gastos com medicamentos e judicializacao ja soma R$ 1 milhao em 2025
summary: Small municipality of Sidrolandia (MS) spent R$1.016 million on judicially ordered medications in first 8 months of 2025, bearing 82% of costs. Receives only R$46,900/month in transfers but spends R$219,700/month of own funds.

title: Judicializacao da saude custou R$ 9,6 bilhoes a Uniao entre 2020 e 2024
summary: Cumulative federal cost of health judicialization between 2020 and 2024 reached R$9.6 billion from 23,046 lawsuits. In 2024 alone, R$2.7 billion -- the highest on record. Eculizumab alone: R$1.77 billion across 2,871 cases.

title: Aumentam os gastos publicos com judicializacao da saude
summary: TCU audit: federal spending on health litigation grew from R$70 million in 2008 to R$1 billion in 2015 -- 1,300% increase. Medication supply accounts for 80% of cases. TCU found measures taken by Ministry and states were insufficient.

title: Decisao judicial nao deve desequilibrar o orcamento, diz Fux
summary: STF Chief Justice Fux relieved municipality of Santa Isabel (SP) from court order to supply eculizumab (~R$860,000/year). Argued solidarity interpretation has deepened inequalities and diverted resources from sanitation and vaccination.

title: STF finaliza acordo sobre judicializacao de remedios de alto custo
summary: STF finalized agreement with federal/state/municipal governments on high-cost medication lawsuits. Monthly health lawsuits rose from 21,000 in 2020 to 61,000 in 2024, totaling ~600,000 annually.

title: Ministerio da Saude volta a ressarcir estados e municipios pela judicializacao de medicamentos
summary: Ministry of Health issued Portaria GM/MS No. 1,805 to resume reimbursing states and municipalities for judicialized medication purchases. Reimbursement had been suspended since 2017.

title: Demandas judiciais relativas a saude crescem 130% em dez anos
summary: CNJ/Insper study: health judicial demands grew 130% between 2008 and 2017 vs 50% for overall litigation. Identified 498,715 first-instance health proceedings across 17 state courts. Ministry spending grew 13-fold in seven years.

title: TJ-RJ recebeu 35 acoes sobre saude por dia nos ultimos 4 anos
summary: TJRJ registered 53,157 health lawsuits between 2021-2025 -- 35 new cases per day. State government (55.4%) and Rio municipality (22.4%) together accounted for 78% of all health lawsuits.

title: MS e vice-campeao brasileiro de judicializacao da Saude
summary: Mato Grosso do Sul is second-highest state for per-capita health lawsuits (behind Federal District). Over 18,500 lawsuits in 2025. During 70-day period, 435 judicialization requests (~6/day).

title: Judicializacao consumiu de 30% a 100% da verba da saude em mais de 250 cidades brasileiras
summary: Using DATAJUD data: in 2020, ~270 municipalities spent 30-100% of entire health budgets on judicialized demands. Nearly half of all 5,569 municipalities allocated up to 10% of health budget to judicial compliance.

title: Judicializacao de medicamentos poe em risco sistema publico de saude
summary: Campinas spent R$47.7 million on court-ordered pharma assistance (2017-2021). 76% involved items absent from SUS lists, 23.7% were state/federal responsibility. Concluded judicialization risks sustainability of municipal health system.

title: Pactuada portaria sobre o ressarcimento de medicamentos judicializados
summary: CIT approved historic portaria for inter-federative reimbursement of court-ordered ANVISA-registered medications. Ministry to begin payments January 2025, acknowledging unsustainable cost burden on subnational governments.

title: Pais busca solucoes para aumento de judicializacao na saude
summary: Senate special report: 130% increase in health lawsuits 2008-2017, spending reaching R$1.6 billion in 2016. R$7 billion/year in judicial sentences means money displaced from other health actions.

title: Judicializacao da Saude (institutional page)
summary: Minas Gerais Health Department: health judicialization consumes ~11% of state health budget. States that when someone sues for specific treatment, resources meant for collective end up going to single case.

title: Governo gasta R$ 2,73 bilhoes com medicamentos fornecidos por decisoes judiciais em 2024
summary: In 2024, Ministry spent R$3.2 billion on judicial medication demands: R$1.9 billion from own budget + R$1.3 billion in reimbursements. 70% of five-year spending went to just ten medications.

title: Labirintos da judicializacao da saude
summary: Analysis: individualized technology-driven model of judicial healthcare undermines constitutional priority of prevention, primary care, and health surveillance. Favors individual demands at expense of structural policies.

title: Os impactos da judicializacao da saude no municipio de Sao Paulo
summary: In 2011, judicialization spending in Sao Paulo = 6% of pharma policy budget, 10% of medication/supplies budget. 55% went toward medications that were state/federal responsibility. Three impacts: unequal access, federative imbalance, budget unpredictability.

title: Perspectivas 2026: Municipio encara desafios na Saude e tenta reduzir filas e sobrecarga
summary: Juiz de Fora (MG) led MG ranking for judicial injunctions on hospitalization/ICU beds. Health Secretary described judicialization as a 'break in the regular flow of bed regulation.' Primary care shows long waits, doctor shortages.

title: Lobby da industria farmaceutica poe direito a saude na UTI
summary: Investigative piece: pharmaceutical industry invests heavily in lobby strategies. Between 2008 and 2015, real growth in medicine budget was 74%, but judicialization of medicines grew 1,006%.

title: A polemica receita da Bancada do Medicamento no Congresso
summary: Exposes informal 'Bancada do Medicamento' -- eight parliamentarians defending pharma interests. Specific deputies received R$150,000 from Interfarma in 2010. Global pharma sector: ~US$1 trillion annual revenue.

title: Com doacoes de R$ 13 mi, industria farmaceutica ganha assento e amplia lobby no novo Congresso
summary: Pharma industry donated R$13 million to campaigns. In 2010/2014 when private financing was allowed: R$26 million and R$57 million to 1,404 candidates. Former Hypera director admitted transferring R$30 million to MDB politicians.

title: Conheca a lei que vai causar prejuizo bilionario ao Ministerio da Saude e ampliar lucro das farmaceuticas
summary: Investigates Article 40 of Industrial Property Law (1997) guaranteeing minimum 10-year patent validity, causing billions in losses to Ministry while amplifying pharma profits. Interfarma and Caeme used judicial actions to maintain monopolies.

outlet: Governo do Estado de Sao Paulo
title: Policia prende quadrilha que fraudou R$ 63 milhoes do Estado (Operacao Garra Rufa)
summary: Criminal network of three pharma labs, an NGO, doctors, and lawyers defrauded R$63 million. Doctors issued improper reports, lawyers filed lawsuits, many patients didn't know suits were filed on their behalf.

title: A judicializacao da Saude: existem interferencias da industria farmaceutica no fenomeno?
summary: Academic research summary showing justice and medicine have been articulated to serve pharma interests. Patient associations are linked to industry. Strong pressure to introduce new medications via judicial demands.

title: Especialistas criticam lobby de fabricantes de medicamentos
summary: Seminar at MG Legislature: experts criticized pharma lobby leading to 'inadequate conduct by healthcare providers.' Evidence of coordinated action between prescribers, lawyers, and pharma.

title: Lobby contra quebra de patentes de medicamentos pagou R$ 1,5 milhao a jornais
summary: Pharma lobby against breaking patents paid R$1.5 million to newspapers for sponsored content. Valor Economico article cost at least R$300,000 for double-page customized content.

title: Medicamentos: Farmaceuticas tentam barrar genericos para cancer
summary: ~50 lawsuits by foreign pharma companies to delay generic versions of ~50 medications for cancer, diabetes, HIV. Judicial strategy to extend patents and block cheaper generics.

title: Acoes judiciais: estrategia da industria farmaceutica para introducao de novos medicamentos
summary: Landmark Chieffi & Barata study: 2,927 judicial actions in SP in 2006. Of 565 legal agents, 549 (97.2%) were private attorneys. 19 lawyers filed ~63% of all lawsuits; for some drugs, one lawyer filed 70% of actions.

title: Ligacoes perigosas: industria farmaceutica, associacoes de pacientes e as batalhas judiciais por acesso a medicamentos
summary: Documents 'dangerous liaisons' between pharma, patient associations, and judicial battles. Connections result from market expansion strategies. Lawsuits increased ~350% in RJ between 2001-2005.

title: Medicos, advogados e industria farmaceutica na judicializacao da saude em Minas Gerais
summary: MG study (1999-2009): single doctor from one law office responsible for ~44% of prescriptions in 117 actions. Greater concentration for newer, more expensive medications. Pharma targets medical students/residents via philanthropy-disguised marketing.

title: Growing demands (Demandas crescentes)
summary: 92% increase in judicial proceedings for medicines over five years. SP state spent R$40 million in 2006-2007 on seven anticancer drugs via court orders, with R$7 million lacking clinical evidence of benefit.

title: Justica determina que Uniao forneca remedio mais caro do mundo para tratamento de bebe com AME
summary: Federal judge ordered Union to provide Zolgensma (~R$12 million) to 4-month-old Benjamin diagnosed with AME. Family had started internet campaign 'Ame o Ben.'

title: Justica autoriza importacao do remedio mais caro do mundo a bebe de 1 ano
summary: Court authorized Zolgensma import (R$12 million) for 1-year-old Isabel with AME. Emphasized Zolgensma's cost-benefit over Spinraza (single application vs lifelong doses).

title: Familia busca ajuda para comprar remedio de R$ 7 milhoes a bebe com doenca rara
summary: Henri with AME couldn't move legs/arms, had respiratory difficulties. Mother mobilized social media for R$7 million Zolgensma. He eventually received it -- 'O Henri renasceu.'

title: Morre bebe com doenca rara que motivou campanha para compra de remedio mais caro do mundo
summary: Baby Aysha died before Zolgensma could be obtained. Highlights life-or-death stakes of delays in accessing high-cost medications.

title: Menino que utilizava remedio mais caro do mundo para tratar doenca rara morre aos 5 anos
summary: Guilherme Martini died at age 5 despite receiving Zolgensma (R$12 million) through judicial action in 2021. Illustrates both successes and limitations of judicial access to high-cost treatments.

title: Menino de 3 anos morre de doenca rara e familia lamenta demora do governo para comprar remedio
summary: 3-year-old Vinicius died from AME. Family blamed government delay in purchasing Zolgensma. Symbol of how bureaucratic delays fulfilling judicial orders can be fatal.

title: Zanin obriga governo a fornecer remedio mais caro do mundo a crianca
summary: STF Minister Zanin confirmed government must provide Zolgensma (~R$6 million) to 2-year-old, overturning STJ denial. Cited 'fundamental rights of the greatest magnitude -- rights to life and health of a child.'

title: Caso Enrico: como age remedio que custa R$ 17 milhoes
summary: 5-year-old Enrico needed Elevidys (R$17 million) for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. STF Minister Gilmar Mendes initially suspended 11 orders (total R$252 million). Agreement eventually reached between Union and Roche.

title: Mae luta na Justica para manter tratamento do filho
summary: Mother fights to maintain Voxzogo (R$1 million/year) for son Antonio with achondroplasia. Treatment began after judicial decision; son began walking. STF suspended supply; mother fears developmental regression.

title: Jovem com doenca rara e fatal nao recebe medicacao ha sete meses
summary: 17-year-old Davi with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome had court order since 2017 guaranteeing eculizumab. Medication undelivered for 7 months due to bureaucratic transfer issues.

title: Cancer: pacientes vao a Justica por acesso a tratamentos sem oferta no SUS
summary: Cintia (47) with advanced breast cancer obtained palbociclib (R$10,000/box) via court. After 9 months regained ability to perform activities she hadn't done in four years.

title: Paciente consegue na Justica fornecimento de medicamento nao disponivel no SUS
summary: Patient with severe eosinophilic asthma facing risk of death obtained medication via court. State argued drug not on essential medicines list. Judge ordered supply within 5 days, R$1,000/day fine.

title: Justica determina o fornecimento de medicamento a homem com doenca degenerativa
summary: Man with familial amyloidotic polyneuropathy obtained Inotersen after Tafamidis (SUS-provided) failed. R$5,000/day fine for non-compliance.

title: Paciente com doenca autoimune rara consegue na Justica medicamento de R$ 14 mil a caixa
summary: Patient with Erdheim-Chester Disease (~500 cases worldwide since 1930) obtained Vemurafenib (R$14,555/box, 4 boxes/month) through Defensoria Publica. Filed same day daughter sought help.

title: Ajude Natalia Pimenta: dirigente do PCO luta contra leucemia rara
summary: Natalia (40) in ICU with rare leukemia needed Revumenib. Injunction denied because drug lacks ANVISA registration. Only proven treatment option -- supporters argue formality violates human dignity.

title: Pais conseguem na Justica remedio para o filho que custa R$ 7 milhoes
summary: After seven months of legal battle, parents obtained Zolgensma (~R$7 million) through SUS. Son now feeds himself, speaks, sits, stands with support.

title: STF define criterios para a concessao judicial de medicamentos nao incorporados ao SUS
summary: Landmark Tema 1234 judgment: courts generally cannot order non-CONITEC medications. Six cumulative conditions required. Judges must consult NAT-Jus, cannot rely solely on prescriptions.

title: Decisao do STF sobre concessao de medicamentos fortalece a ciencia e reforca o papel coletivo do SUS
summary: Ministry created dedicated judicialization department and national platform. CONITEC brought into Fonajus. Minister Nisia called decision 'a milestone for Brazil and for SUS.'

title: Decisao do STF pode organizar judicializacao sobre acesso a medicamentos mas fortalecimento da Conitec e criticado
summary: STF decision may organize judicialization but patient associations and pharma criticize 'undisputed power' given to CONITEC. Concerns about transparency and Ministry influence on evaluations.

title: Forum do Judiciario para a Saude aprova medidas para reducao da judicializacao
summary: Under Minister Barroso, Fonajus approved working group for e-NatJus improvement, itinerant Fonajus to visit courts, 120-day deadline for state health committees to develop plans.

title: CNJ e ANS assinam acordo para reducao da judicializacao da saude suplementar
summary: Cooperation agreement to prevent new supplementary health lawsuits, speed case processing, provide technical-scientific support. Over 330,000 active lawsuits involve health plan operators.

title: Bases de dados tecnicos de saude devem ser integradas ao e-NatJus 4.0
summary: e-NatJus 4.0: ~240,000 technical notes supporting 183,000 health cases. Consolidating multiple health databases into single platform for evidence-based judicial decisions.

title: Sistema do e-Natjus refina busca de notas e pareceres tecnicos em saude
summary: CNJ improved e-NatJus search functionality. Platform had accumulated over 88,000 notes. Refinement aimed to support growing judicial demand for evidence-based health decisions.

title: NAT-Jus/SP alcanca marca de 1 mil notas tecnicas na biblioteca digital
summary: SP NAT-Jus reached 1,000 technical notes milestone. Notes produced by health professionals to guide judges on clinical questions about medications, treatments, procedures.

title: TJSC expande emissao de notas tecnicas por meio do NatJus para as 112 comarcas
summary: Santa Catarina expanding NatJus to all 112 municipalities by Nov 2025 (pilot March 2025). Evidence-based notes via telehealth professionals from Funmed.

title: TRF4 implanta as primeiras varas federais do pais especializadas em saude
summary: First federal courts specialized in health: 3rd Federal Court of Curitiba and four in Porto Alegre. Responded to CNJ Recommendation No. 43.

title: Judicializacao da saude: Goiania ganha duas varas especializadas
summary: Goiania installed two courts dedicated to health litigation, part of national movement for specialized judicial units following CNJ Recommendation No. 43.

title: 9a e 15a Varas da Fazenda Publica de Fortaleza serao exclusivas para demandas de saude
summary: Ceara converted two courts to handle exclusively public health demands. ~2,500 pending cases to be distributed. Established Nucleo de Justica 4.0 for public health.

title: Camara de Resolucao de Litigios em Saude comemora 12 anos
summary: RJ CRLS (2013-2025): analyzed 201,700+ requests, 57.52% resolved without litigation. Extrajudicial resolution rate climbed from ~35% (2013-14) to ~63% (2022-23). Savings of at least R$3.5 million.

title: Camara de Resolucao Extrajudicial de Litigios de Saude completa primeiro ano
summary: Amazonas extrajudicial chamber resolved 89.7% of demands without litigation in first year, saving R$1.78 million.

title: Tribunal do Para instala em Belem CEJUSC especializado em saude
summary: TJPA established specialized health CEJUSC in Belem with statewide competence. First conciliation session resolved ICU bed/surgery case.

title: Diagnostico do CNJ aponta alto indice de deferimento de pedidos em saude e baixa conciliacao
summary: CNJ diagnostic: ~600,000 health lawsuits filed Jan 2024 - Aug 2025. Six states show injunction approval rates above 85%. Conciliation rates below 1% in 17 states.

title: Judicializacao reforca desigualdade entre clientes de planos de saude
summary: UFMG study: health plan clients who judicialize most frequently held individual plans, lived in wealthy areas, had broader provider networks. Judicializing more accessible to wealthier citizens.

title: Luta pela vida, reforco da desigualdade ou gasto desenfreado?
summary: SP 2010-2014: of 56,000 cases, 64% filed by private lawyers (only 13.8% public defenders), nearly half of prescriptions from private doctors. Success rates exceed 80% but procedural costs exclude poorest.

title: 5 fatos surpreendentes sobre a judicializacao da saude no Brasil
summary: Reports 'paradoxical inequality': judicialization may deepen inequalities as those with more resources access justice more easily. Massive regional heterogeneity. Collective actions underutilized but yield 7% higher success.

outlet: International Journal for Equity in Health
title: (Un)Equitable distribution of health resources and the judicialization of healthcare: 10 years of experience in Brazil
summary: 10-year analysis finds 'contrary positive discrimination tendency -- in favor of advantaged groups.' Access to courts skewed toward people with comparatively better health conditions due to economic situation.

title: The right to health in the courts of Brazil: Worsening health inequities?
summary: Examines whether judicial enforcement worsens health inequities. Growing proportion of cases from supplementary insurance (25% of population, wealthier) and small role of public defenders suggest regressive pattern.

outlet: International Journal for Equity in Health
title: Is the judicialization of health care bad for equity? A scoping review
summary: Scoping review: evidence on regressivity inconclusive. Some studies find majority of litigants are poor/older individuals. Others show concentration in developed areas and high-cost medicines. Calls for more rigorous methodology.

title: Infografico apresenta panoramas da Judicializacao da Saude e da Medicina no Brasil
summary: Massive regional disparity: South has 5.11 cases per 1,000 inhabitants vs 0.80 in North. SP leads with 133,500 cases. Health litigation grew 198% over nine years while general litigation fell 6%.

title: Right-to-Medicines Litigation and Universal Health Coverage: Institutional Determinants of the Judicialization of Health in Brazil
summary: Presence of Public Defender's Office is a major determinant of whether judicialization occurs. Municipalities without public defenders -- typically poorer/remote -- see far less litigation.

title: Pesquisa avalia interferencia da industria farmaceutica na judicializacao da saude
summary: UFMG doctoral research: patients obtain high-cost treatments that aren't always best options but generate profit for lawyers, doctors, pharma. MG spent R$290 million on judicial health actions in 2016. Purpose of resolving public policy problem ended up favoring pharma profits.

title: Apos decisao do STF sobre judicializacao, instituicoes se mobilizam em busca de dialogo mais profundo
summary: After STF Tema 1234 decision, patient associations (Abrale, Abrasta, Febrararas) mobilized politically, requesting CNJ meetings and seeking Congressional alternatives. Associations act as organized political players.

title: Judicializacao: no STF ministra Nisia afirma: 'esse e um marco para o Brasil e para o SUS'
summary: Health Minister celebrated STF Tema 1234 as victory for executive branch regaining control over pharmaceutical policy. Medicines approved by Anvisa but not in SUS can only be ordered under strict conditions.

title: Judicialization and right to health in Brazil: a trajectory of matches and mismatches
summary: Comprehensive review of three-decade trajectory. Divide between pro-litigation camp (guaranteeing equitable rights) and anti-litigation camp (deepening inequalities). Ongoing political contest over legitimacy of judicial intervention.

title: Justica determina bloqueio de verbas para fornecer remedio a paciente com cancer
summary: Judge in Caico (RN) blocked state funds to supply kidney cancer medication. Illustrates judges' power to sequester public budgets when states fail to provide court-ordered treatments.

title: Justica mantem bloqueio de R$ 325 milhoes da prefeitura do Rio
summary: TRT-RJ froze R$325 million from Rio de Janeiro municipality accounts to pay 20,000+ outsourced health workers (community agents, pharmacists, nursing techs) with salaries unpaid since October 2019.

title: Fazenda publica pode ser multada por nao fornecer medicamento
summary: STJ Tema 98: First Section unanimously ruled daily fines (astreintes) can be imposed on government for non-compliance with medication supply orders. RS case: glaucoma patient won half-minimum-wage daily fine.

title: STF nega sequestro de precatorios para doencas graves
summary: STF limited sequestration of precatorios (court-ordered government debts) for health cases, even serious diseases. Balanced individual urgency against fiscal responsibility. Only allowed when no budgetary allocation exists.

title: TCE multa ex-prefeito Dr. Pessoa por descumprir decisao sobre recursos da saude
summary: TCE-PI fined Teresina ex-mayor 5,000 UFR-PI for non-compliance with health budget precautionary measures during 2023. Mayor failed to present defense or prove compliance. Shows audit courts also enforce health spending rules.

title: Paciente em risco de rompimento de aneurisma esta ha quase 100 dias internada sem cirurgia no SUS-MG
summary: Elizabete Fernandes, 44, hospitalized 100 days in MG with cerebral aneurysm risk. Hospital lacked SUS credentialing for endovascular surgery. Transfer via CINT Belo Horizonte ordered Dec 3 but never executed. Lawsuit seeks judicial fund seizure for private surgery.

title: Espera de quase 10 anos na fila de cirurgia gera indenizacao a paciente da rede publica de saude
summary: DF condemned to R$20k damages for child waiting nearly 10 years for cranial surgery that should be done in infancy. Court recognized state negligence via omission -- failing to provide care the SUS promises.

title: Falta de medicamentos atinge 80% das cidades brasileiras
summary: CNM survey of 3,360 municipalities: 80% reported medicine shortages. 68% lacked amoxicillin, 66% lacked dipirona. 1,392 municipalities resorted to emergency procurement. Ministry admitted low stock of ~90 substances including antibiotics, saline solution.

title: Falta de medicamentos atinge mais de 80% das cidades
summary: Fiocruz analysis: SUS medicine shortages are structural, not temporary. Brazil's domestic pharmaceutical ingredient production fell from 50% to 5% of needs over 40 years. 2017 financing reform reduced 6 blocks to 2, fragmenting the system.

title: SUS waiting lists: 1.6 million Brazilians await surgery
summary: 1.6 million Brazilians on SUS surgical waiting lists. 5% die per year of waiting. Patients waiting 7 years have 18% higher mortality than those operated immediately. UK comparison: no one waits >18 weeks, 90% operated within that period.

title: Liminar aponta 'afronta a concorrencia' em compra para doencas raras
summary: Rare disease drug distribution monopoly: ANVISA resolution required manufacturer authorization for importers, creating single-distributor monopolies. Federal judge ruled this violated bidding competition principles. 2010-2015: R$2.7B spent judicially, 54% on just 3 drugs (Elaprase, Naglazyme, Soliris).

title: Tribunal fiscaliza gestao de demandas judiciais de medicamento
summary: TCU audit found R$26.4 million in judicially purchased medicines expired between 2018-2022. Emergency procurement without competitive bidding leads to systematic waste. Highlights inefficiency of individualized judicial purchasing vs. centralized procurement.

title: Medicamentos nao incorporados mais judicializados no SUS sao para doencas raras
summary: Top non-incorporated judicially mandated drugs: vosoritida (achondroplasia) R$875M and atalureno (Duchenne) R$765M between 2022-2024. Pharma companies delay incorporation requests while litigation forces purchase at full price. BioMarin only planning Conitec submission for 2025.

title: Remedio de R$ 6,5 milhoes: preco baseado na cura e injusto e cruel
summary: IDEC criticized CMED for raising Zolgensma from R$2.9M to R$6.5M using 'value-based pricing' (comparing to years of competitor Spinraza). Families forced to sue for access. Later resolved: SUS adopted risk-sharing agreement, achieving lowest global price.

title: SUS realiza primeiras aplicacoes do Zolgensma via acordo de compartilhamento de risco
summary: SUS began providing Zolgensma (~R$7M) through innovative risk-sharing agreement: payment only if treatment is effective. Brazil secured lowest list price globally. Shows how incorporation can resolve judicialization -- prior to this, families had to sue.

title: Mapa da Defensoria mostra que faltam defensores em 72% das comarcas
summary: IPEA/ANADEP 'Mapa da Defensoria': public defenders absent from 72% of 2,680 comarcas. Only 5,054 of 8,489 positions filled (59.5%). Deficit most severe in small districts (<100k pop) with lower HDI. Total deficit: 10,578 defenders.

title: Brasil esta longe de colocar Defensoria em todas as comarcas
summary: Despite Constitutional Amendment 80/2014 deadline, 41% of state comarcas and 60% of federal subsections still lacked public defenders as of June 2024. Coverage rose from 47% to 59.1% between 2021 and 2024 -- still far from universal.

title: Biehl et al: right to medicines litigation in Rio Grande do Sul
summary: Princeton/Johns Hopkins study of 1,262 lawsuits in RS: presence of Defensoria associated with 7x increase in probability of municipality having medicine lawsuit. Demonstrates that access to legal representation -- not just disease burden -- drives litigation geography.

title: Advogados privados lideram 64% das acoes de saude em SP
summary: Chieffi SP data 2010-2014: of 56,000 health lawsuits, private lawyers led 64%, Defensoria only 13.8%, prosecutors 9%. Of 20 most demanded drugs, only 4 lacked SUS alternatives. 63% increase in volume over period. 'Judicialization accentuates inequality in access.'

title: Defensoria celebra dois anos da CRELS com R$ 12 milhoes economizados e 92.5% de resolutividade
summary: Amazonas CRELS (health litigation resolution chamber): 4,278 demands handled in 2 years, 92.5% resolution rate, R$12.5M saved. Meanwhile DPE-AM has deficit of 80 positions, budget frozen since 2021 at 0.69% of state budget.

title: Os impactos da judicializacao da saude no municipio de Sao Paulo: gasto publico e organizacao federativa
summary: SP DJES study: judicialization consumed 6% of municipal pharmaceutical budget and 10% of hospital supplies budget. 55% of judicial costs were for medicines that were responsibility of other government levels (state/Union). SP created dedicated department in 2020.

title: Camara de Conciliacao de Saude resolve 80% dos casos na Bahia
summary: Bahia's CCS achieved 80% resolution rate within 9 months of establishment. Brings together Defensoria and health secretariats to resolve medication/treatment requests without litigation. Jan-Jul 2024: 3,409 visits, 4,164 assessments.

title: Campo Grande cria Catjus e economiza R$ 425 mil em dois meses
summary: Campo Grande spends ~R$26M/year on health judicialization. Created Catjus (Coordenacao de Apoio Tecnico a Judicializacao da Saude) which saved R$425k in Jul-Aug alone by redirecting patients to existing SUS services.

title: Nucleo diminui judicializacoes na area da saude em Joinville
summary: Joinville NAT-Jus (est. 2016): peak judicial spending R$10.4M in 2016. New actions fell from 227 (2017) to 144 (2018) -- 36.6% decline. 20% of cases resolved via patient guidance, 35% resolved without litigation. Collective actions dropped from 13 to 1.

title: Ministerio da Saude volta a ressarcir estados e municipios pela judicializacao de medicamentos
summary: Federal reimbursement resumed after 6-year suspension (2017-2023). First states: SC, RS, PR, ES, MS, CE, PE. Dec 2024 CIT Portaria: Union reimburses 65% (80% for oncology), back-payments for 2018-2024 within 5 years.

title: Experiencia exitosa do Parana para diminuir demandas judiciais de medicamentos
summary: Parana spends R$300M/year on judicial health demands. Pioneered PREC pre-judicialization project and reimbursement mechanism: state buys Union-responsibility drugs, fixes price via Cemepar, obtains federal reimbursement. Recognized as national model.

title: Camara de Conciliacao em Saude amplia atendimentos
summary: Vitoria da Conquista created pioneering CCS in Bahia (March 2022) via Technical Cooperation Agreement between municipal health and Defensoria. Restructured 2023 to expand legal team to 2 days/week. Resolves medication/treatment requests without litigation.

title: Avalanche de acoes judiciais na saude so cresce e desorganiza orcamento em MS
summary: MS health lawsuits rose from 6,500 (2023) to 7,659 (2024), with 810 new actions by Feb 2025 alone. State prosecutor described it as 'seizure' of public resources. Makes planned health policy execution impossible.

title: Nao lido com o cofre diz ministra do STF sobre judicializacao da saude
summary: STF President Carmen Lucia: 'I deal with the human not the treasury.' Health Minister Barros: 'judicial action displaces resources.' 80% of actions for one drug from single law firm. Hypercholesterolemia fraud: R$36M doctors paid R$300/prescription. NAT-Jus platform launched.

title: SUS nao entrega ao menos 76 medicamentos e procedimentos incorporados a rede publica desde 2018
summary: 76 of 242 CONITEC-incorporated items (31.4%) unavailable after average 648 days -- three times the legal deadline. Insulin analog incorporated 2019 unavailable after 2000+ days. Reasons: unsigned contracts missing protocols pending CIT. Baby Manuella (Acre) died before treatment available.

title: Um unico remedio custou ao SUS R$ 2.44 bilhoes em 11 anos revela estudo
summary: Eculizumab cost SUS R$2.44B over 11 years. Single law firm filed ~70% of 514 federal actions; 73% originated in DF. Of 414 patients roughly half lacked confirmed diagnosis. Operacao Calice de Higia (2017): purchases fell 49.5%. Price dropped 35% after ANVISA registration.

title: Pedidos de remedio na Justica caem e SP evita gastos de R$ 205 milhoes
summary: First decline in a decade: SP judicial health spending from R$1.09B to R$887M (16% drop 27% for Defensoria cases). Acessa SUS pre-litigation program. 1 in 4 judicially ordered drugs already on SUS list. R$40M fraud scheme uncovered in 2015.

title: Governo Bolsonaro incinerou medicamentos de alto custo para doencas raras
summary: R$13.5M in rare disease drugs incinerated: Translarna R$2.74M eculizumab R$1.73M Spinraza R$319k. Total R$214.2M health products discarded since 2019. Stock data classified since 2018. Municipalities forced to buy via emergency procurement while federal stockpiles destroyed.

title: Governo federal gasta R$ 575 mi na compra de tres remedios para doencas raras por ordens judiciais
summary: Top 3 drugs = 53.25% of R$1.1B: Translarna R$257M Soliris R$216M Zolgensma R$101M. Total 2022: R$1.6B (up 335% from 2012). 50000+ active federal lawsuits. Zolgensma incorporated Dec 2022 but unavailable 9 months later.

title: A mafia da judicializacao da saude
summary: Op-ed by Pedro Ramos. Describes Operacao Mr. Hyde: unnecessary surgeries with low-quality materials. Fraud ranges from trivial items to expensive unregistered drugs. Organized networks of doctors lawyers and pharma representatives.

title: Ministerio da Saude paga R$ 2.7 bilhoes com medicamentos judicializados e teme explosao de custos
summary: R$1.8B (2022) to R$2.73B (2024) rising ~R$400M/year. Elevidys: R$14.6M/dose ANVISA registration suspended but courts still ordering. R$3B needed for 213 active Elevidys lawsuits. Conitec rejected: gains dont exceed corticosteroids. Zolgensma risk-sharing March 2025.

title: O Complexo: Parte II -- O dinheiro sempre
summary: Investigative dossier on SUS underfunding. Ministry analysis: R$77B federal funding gap. Federal share fell from 45.3% (2012) to 37.6% (2022). EC 95/2016 spending ceiling cost SUS ~R$76B (2018-2022). Previne Brasil disrupted primary care. Tax subsidies to private health sector: R$70.7B.

title: Farra ilimitada
summary: Secret budget (orcamento secreto) fraud in SUS. Municipalities inflated procedure counts: 540k tooth extractions in city of 38k. Parliamentary kickbacks up to 30%. Maranhao attracted R$918M. SUS audits collapsed from 1300/year to 151. Baby Gael died -- hospital lacked pediatrician incubator neonatal ICU despite city receiving millions.

title: Gasto do governo com remedio sem aval da Anvisa cresce 220 vezes em 5 anos
summary: Non-ANVISA-registered drug spending grew 220x in 5 years: R$2.4M in 2010 (2% of R$122M total) to R$545M in 2015 (50% of R$1.1B total). Cancer drugs rare disease treatments hepatitis C and cannabidiol products drove growth. STF judging Tema 500 on obligation to provide non-registered drugs.

title: Governos gastam R$ 314 milhoes com remedio importado
summary: R$314M spent on imported drugs from judicial decisions in 2014 forcing state and Union to purchase medications without ANVISA registration. Documents fiscal cost of judicially mandated imports.

title: Com judicializacao da saude juizes passam a ditar politicas publicas do setor
summary: Judge Galhardo created pre-litigation committee in Araraquara reducing health lawsuits 70% (Innovare Prize 2007). Desembargador Dip: 'How can we deny when state defenses are generic?' TJSP handled 40000+ health cases/year costing SP over R$1B.

title: Solucoes construidas pelo CNJ buscam reduzir judicializacao da saude
summary: Judges describe core dilemma: 'We are deciding under pressure about a subject we do not master because we are not doctors.' Receive one-sided petitions with urgency requests must decide immediately. Documents decade of CNJ institutional responses including National Health Forum and NAT-Jus.

title: Judicializacao da saude no Brasil: Impacto desafios e papel do NatJus
summary: NAT-Jus data from Roraima (2019-2024): only 12.3% of cases classified as urgent were genuinely urgent vs 66.5% non-urgent. Goias: 18.1% truly urgent vs 81.9% not. Many judges resist NAT-Jus consultation citing urgency judicial autonomy or missing infrastructure. 53.8% of NAT-Jus opinions fully favorable to patient.

title: Prazo de 180 dias para oferta de novos medicamentos via de regra nao e cumprido
summary: CGU audit of 25 medications: zero met 180-day legal deadline. Average delay 624 days. Financing-definition stage alone ~300 days; gap from financing to first acquisition ~265 days. Maximum observed delay: 1314 days (3.6 years). Created Monitor dos 180 Dias tracking 900+ incorporation cases since 2012.

title: Pharmaceutical industry interference in CONITEC incorporation process (Tamachiro et al)
summary: Study of 514 incorporation requests (2012-2020): 37% from pharma companies; industry provided 70.7% of all public consultation contributions. One submission (nusinersena) generated 41787 contributions. Companies deliberately avoid CONITEC when evidence is weak preferring judicialization. 52.7% of industry requests rejected.

title: Critical analysis of nusinersena/Spinraza incorporation into SUS (Caetano et al)
summary: CONITEC unanimously rejected nusinersena in Nov 2018. After Attorney General intervention second submission approved March 2019 with no new clinical evidence. Public consultation: 41787 contributions in 10 days (56% of all contributions across 123 favorable recommendations 2012-2019). Federal spending: ~R$118M for 496 units in 2018.

title: Empresa com apenas 1 funcionario leva contrato de R$ 285.8 mi na Saude
summary: Auramedi Farmaceutica -- micro-enterprise with 1 employee and R$1.3M capital -- won R$285.8M contract without bidding for immunoglobulin. HQ found closed and without employees during business hours. Owner defendant in pandemic-era fraud case. Co-representative linked to Operacao Vampiro (2004).

title: Justica acolhe pedido da AGE-MG e determina bloqueio por superfaturamento de Trikafta
summary: Two importers overcharged ~R$2M for Trikafta (cystic fibrosis). Court froze R$5.3M and pierced corporate veil. Companies sold without ANVISA authorization. Market price ~R$650k vs prices charged far above.

title: Anemia falciforme foi invisibilizada pelo racismo apontam entidades
summary: ~100000 patients with sickle cell disease in Brazil; 95% are Black. 30000+ preventable deaths annually. Most are Bolsa Familia beneficiaries. No SUS protocols until 2005 despite century of diagnosis. Ministry: institutional racism affects care quality for this population.

title: Judicializacao da saude: um ano do julgamento do Tema 1234 do STF
summary: One-year retrospective: SUS lawsuits declined ~6-7% in H1 2025. NatJus notes for non-incorporated drugs up 40%. Union reimbursement claims rose 878%. National Health Platform delivered to CNJ Jan 2026 (15 months post-decision). Supplementary health lawsuits rose 7% (opposite direction).

title: STF precisou reforcar a aplicacao das Sumulas Vinculantes 60 e 61
summary: STF intervened twice in 2025 to enforce compliance with Tema 1234. Problems: judges ordering direct patient reimbursement (now prohibited); courts not enforcing PMVG price ceiling; CMED needing updated sanctions. Recommended expanding judicial education on health matters.

title: Uso de notas tecnicas para embasar decisoes judiciais em saude cresce cerca de 32% em 2025
summary: NAT-Jus technical notes grew 32% in 2025 (~131000 vs ~99000 in 2024). e-NatJus system now houses over 394000 technical notes total. Indicates increased judicial consultation of medical evidence following Tema 1234 decision.

title: Apos decisao do STF 19.8% tiveram tratamentos interrompidos
summary: Interfarma survey post-STF Tema 1234: 53.8% of patients continued treatment; 26.3% supply denied uncertain or pending; 19.8% had judicially-ordered treatments interrupted. Rare disease lawsuits grew 21.3% between 2022-2024 despite reforms.

title: Judicializacao soma 1.49% dos custos dos planos de saude
summary: ANS data: judicial costs = R$3.9B in Q1 2025 (1.49% of total expenses). Tripled since 2020 (R$1.2B/0.65%). 62% of judicial demands involve procedures already in mandatory coverage. Operators earned R$7.1B profit in Q1 2025 (+114% vs 2024). 231k new lawsuits against plans Aug 2024-Jul 2025.
